note: Presentation only. Which stage of the case-study track each outcome in edges.json is drawn against. This is the author's reading of where in the process an outcome shows up, not a sourced claim; it adds no edge and sets no lag. Edit by hand. lever_stage is the stage at which each lever is set; planner_stage is where a planner or advocate steps into the process. Both are the author's reading and are to be tested in user session 1. decision_timing says, per decision, whether timing.json has a duration it acts on; decision_stack and fact_callouts place the callouts on the sheet. gap_step gives, for each pair of neighbouring stages, the timing.json step that fills the gap and its weeks; the page draws that gap on a log scale. range gives, per decision, the order its settings sit in on the lever (a presentation order, not a scale) and the setting in force now where edges.json says so. A lever has detents, not a continuous range: there is no sourced effect between two settings. The permit lever shows allow and minor repair only; deny has no sourced edge and none of the seven cases was refused, so it is left off the sheet (edges.json still lists it). outcome_who says who an effect lands on (T tenants, N neighbourhood, C City and owners, B buildings); it is the author's reading and is not sourced.
